content: Abciximab, commercially known as ReoPro®, is the Fab fragment derived from the chimeric human-murine monoclonal antibody 7E3. This agent specifically binds to the glycoprotein (GP) IIb/IIIa receptor located on human platelets, effectively inhibiting platelet aggregation. Additionally, abciximab exhibits binding affinity for the vitronectin receptor (αvβ3), which is expressed on platelets, endothelial cells lining vessel walls, and smooth muscle cells. The chimeric 7E3 antibody is produced through continuous perfusion in mammalian cell culture systems. The resulting Fab fragment, with a molecular weight of 47,615 daltons, undergoes a rigorous purification process. This includes specific viral inactivation and removal procedures, enzymatic digestion with papain, and subsequent column chromatography. ReoPro® is formulated as a clear, colorless, sterile, and non-pyrogenic solution intended for intravenous (IV) administration. The solution contains 0.001% polysorbate 80 in Water for Injection, with no added preservatives. When administered at a dose of 30 mg/kg, abciximab produces a rapid, dose-dependent inhibition of platelet function. This effect is measured ex vivo by assessing platelet aggregation in response to adenosine diphosphate (ADP) or by observing a prolongation in bleeding time. At two hours post-injection, which was the earliest time point evaluated, over 80% of GP IIb/IIIa receptors were blocked, and platelet aggregation in response to 20 μM ADP was nearly completely suppressed. Furthermore, the median bleeding time increased significantly to over 30 minutes at both evaluated doses, compared to a baseline bleeding time of approximately five minutes.
